claims.claim: **Use as first systemic therapy for advanced or unresectable HCC that cannot be treated curatively or locoregionally**, when the disease is BCLC B or C, liver function is Child-Pugh class A, performance status is ECOG 0 or 1, and varices have been checked by endoscopy within the last 6 months.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Start only under specialists experienced with immunotherapy who can manage immune-related toxicity,** and decide it with a multidisciplinary team that includes a gastroenterologist and a medical oncologist.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use clinical judgement and expert discussion if the patient has** significant autoimmune disease, an organ transplant, previous viral hepatitis or previous lung irradiation.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The pivotal trial excluded** autoimmune disease, untreated or partly treated oesophageal or gastric varices, and therapeutic anticoagulant or antiplatelet treatment (low-dose aspirin was allowed).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fatal variceal bleeding risk.** Look for gastro-oesophageal varices and treat them as needed within 6 months before the first dose. Do not start if varices are untreated, bleeding now or recently, high-risk, or have not been checked in the past 6 months.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Caution with blood thinners:** current use of full-dose anticoagulants, thrombolytics or antiplatelet drugs, or use within 10 days before starting.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Screen every patient for hepatitis before a checkpoint inhibitor.** Patients with chronic hepatitis B or C, a detectable HIV viral load or AIDS need close monitoring and antiviral treatment where indicated.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Get blood pressure under control before bevacizumab** and keep monitoring it; start or adjust antihypertensives as needed. Do a baseline urine test for protein.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If steroids are needed before treatment, keep the dose as low as possible** (ideally no more than 10 mg prednisolone equivalent a day).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Regimen:** atezolizumab 1,200 mg IV plus bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV, both on day 1 of a 21-day cycle, continued until progression or unacceptable toxicity. The first infusions run over 60 minutes (atezolizumab) and 90 minutes (bevacizumab), and later doses can be shortened to 30 minutes if tolerated.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Alternatives:** atezolizumab may be given subcutaneously (1,875 mg every 21 days). If bevacizumab is stopped, atezolizumab can continue alone, with an alternative IV schedule of 1680 mg every 28 days.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Do not dose-reduce the checkpoint inhibitor.** No adjustment is needed for older age or mild hepatic impairment; moderate to severe hepatic impairment has not been studied.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Early growth on scans may be pseudo-progression** (rare, about 5%). If the patient seems to be benefiting, consider carrying on and repeating the scan after 4 to 6 weeks before calling it progression.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Bloods:** FBC, EUC, eGFR, LFTs, cortisol, thyroid function and glucose at baseline; FBC, EUC, eGFR, LFTs and glucose before every cycle; thyroid function every 4–6 weeks on treatment and 12-weekly afterwards (consider cortisol on the same schedule).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Check urine protein periodically (for example every 3 to 4 months)** or if there is oedema or unexplained low albumin; significant proteinuria (above 3 g/L) may need a treatment break.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Immune-related adverse events can start early, worsen fast, and appear after treatment stops; some are fatal.** Monitor actively, teach patients to report symptoms early, and manage with interruption or cessation, specialist input and corticosteroids.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Around surgery:** hold bevacizumab for at least 28 days before elective surgery and restart no sooner than 28 days afterwards, once the wound has healed.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Stop bevacizumab permanently for:** grade 3 or worse haemorrhage; life-threatening venous thromboembolism, pulmonary embolism, stroke or arterial insufficiency; arterial thromboembolism; grade 4 or persistent grade 3 hypertension; nephrotic syndrome; GI perforation or fistula; or reversible posterior leukoencephalopathy.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Survival benefit over sorafenib:** in a phase III trial of 501 patients, median overall survival was 19.2 months with atezolizumab plus bevacizumab versus 13.4 months with sorafenib (HR 0.66).
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Progression-free survival and response were also better:** median PFS 6.9 vs 4.3 months; confirmed response 30% vs 11%, with complete response in 8%.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Toxicity was similar and quality of life held up longer:** grade 3–4 treatment-related events 43% vs 46%; time to quality-of-life deterioration 11.2 vs 3.6 months.
claims.locator: eviQ Cancer Treatments Online, Cancer Institute NSW, '3881 HCC advanced or metastatic atezolizumab and bevacizumab (eviQ ID 3881, version 5)', first approved 2 November 2020; last reviewed 1 August 2025; review due 31 December 2029, https://www.eviq.org.au/p/3881, retrieved 2026-09-23
